headline: NAMIBIA COPPER ASSAYS CONFIRMED: KAOKO METALS HITS 37M AT 1.23% CU WITH 3.05% HIGH-GRADE CORE
snippet: First lab-confirmed assays from Chalkos Project, Namibia: 37.1m @ 1.23% Cu (incl. 6.62m @ 3.05% Cu, 40g/t Ag) and 48m @ 1.02% Cu. Kaoko Metals (ASX: KAO) previously reported only visual intercepts — these are the first quantified grades. Company raised A$20M to accelerate drilling at what analysts are calling a potential large-tonnage copper-silver discovery in Namibia's emerging copper belt.

headline: MIDAS MINERALS STRETCHES SPAATZU COPPER ZONE TO 1.5KM — 51M AT 0.82% CU OPEN TO SOUTHEAST
snippet: Latest hole intercepts 51m @ 0.82% Cu at the Spaatzu project in Namibia's emerging copper belt, extending mineralised strike to 1.5km and leaving the system open to the southeast. Midas Minerals (ASX: MM1) is part of a wave of ASX-listed explorers targeting Namibia's under-drilled copper corridor, which is drawing comparisons to the Kalahari Copper Belt in Botswana.

headline: QMINES HITS COPPER SULPHIDES 180M BEYOND MT CHALMERS RESOURCE BOUNDARY — ASSAYS DUE LATE OCTOBER
snippet: Diamond hole 26MCDD052 intersects 11m of visual chalcopyrite-pyrite stringers 180m beyond the current resource envelope at Mt Chalmers, Queensland. QMines (ASX: QML) expects assays by late October; if confirmed, the hit pushes the Cu-Au-Ag system into new ground. Defined resource sits at 12.6Mt grading 1.0% CuEq. Follows a recent feasibility update that moved the project toward a development decision.

headline: CALEDONIA SLASHES BLANKET MINE GOLD GUIDANCE TO 69K OZ — COMPRESSED AIR FAILURE HITS DEEP HIGH-GRADE ZONES
snippet: Caledonia Mining (LSE/NYSE: CMCL) cuts 2026 guidance to 69,000–72,500 oz from 72,000–76,500 oz after Q3 production slipped to 17,030 oz (vs 19,106 oz prior year). Root cause: insufficient compressed-air capacity in deeper high-grade sections at Blanket Mine, Zimbabwe. Shares fell 5.6% in London. Management expects Q4 recovery from new compressor capacity and roughly 1,100 oz from a circuit release mid-October.

headline: GALIANO GOLD LOCKS IN ASANKO MINE LEASES THROUGH 2043 — GHANA GRANTS 15-17 YEAR EXTENSIONS
snippet: Ghana approves two major lease renewals at Asanko Gold Mine: Abirem Mining Lease extended 15 years to 2041; Miradani Mining Lease extended 17 years to 2043. Galiano Gold (TSX: GAU) calls the renewals a platform for reserve growth at its 5.8 Mtpa processing plant covering the Nkran, Adubiaso, and Miradani North deposits. Approvals remove a key long-term uncertainty ahead of a planned resource expansion program.

headline: COT DATA: SILVER SPECS TURN BULLISH AS GOLD LONGS WEAKEN — FOMC MEETING OCT 27 IS NEXT KEY CATALYST
snippet: Published Oct 11: CFTC Commitments of Traders analysis shows silver speculative positioning shifting bullish (~105,000 contracts) while gold net longs remain elevated but show early signs of weakening. Gold retreated below $4,200 late in the week after spiking on Oct 9 jobs data. The Oct 27–28 FOMC meeting is flagged as the next macro catalyst likely to resolve the near-term directional uncertainty in precious metals.

headline: GOLDSEEK COT REVIEW: GOLD BULLS INTACT BUT FADING — SILVER REBUILDS SPEC LONGS FROM HISTORIC LOWS
snippet: Gold large-spec net longs remain well above shorts but not at historically extreme levels signalling capitulation. The standout signal: silver specs are rebuilding long positions from multi-year lows set during September's correction, a development GoldSeek's analysts flag as a potential contrarian accumulation signal. Spot gold near $4,190, silver near $61.50. USDX positioning neutral. Published Oct 9 with CFTC data through Oct 6.

headline: WELDON: MODELS SAY SELL GOLD BUT HE WON'T BET AGAINST IT — TARGETS $8,500-$10,000 ON FED DEBT SURRENDER
snippet: Macro veteran Greg Weldon says his short-term trading models are flashing a sell signal on gold but he refuses to act on it given the structural fiscal picture. Long-term target: $8,500–$10,000/oz, driven by what he calls 'Washington's Gold Thief' — compounding federal deficits as a structural gold driver. Published Oct 9 as gold bounced on jobs data. Weldon argues the Fed has already surrendered its inflation mandate to avoid a debt spiral.
